strengths: Novel theoretical contribution: Theorem 3.1 establishes exact equivalence between local-SSL and BP-SSL gradients for deep linear networks with orthonormal weights, providing genuine insight into when local learning matches global learning

Theory-guided algorithm development: Systematic progression from theoretical insights (linear networks) to practical algorithms (spatially dependent B^l in convnets) with proper ablations demonstrating each component's contribution

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets with confidence intervals, gradient alignment metrics validating theory, careful ablation studies (Figure 5) showing contributions of each algorithmic component
Unified notation framework: Table 1 elegantly unifies multiple local-SSL algorithms (CLAPP, Forward-forward, SCFF, PhyLL), facilitating analysis and comparison across methods
Achieves state-of-the-art local-SSL performance: CLAPP++ variants reach or exceed previous best local-SSL methods on CIFAR-10, STL-10, and Tiny ImageNet while providing theoretical justification
Thorough reproducibility: Detailed appendices with training procedures, network architectures, hyperparameters, and datasets enable reproduction
weaknesses: Severe theory-practice gap: Theorem 3.1 requires orthonormal weights (constant layer sizes) and linear networks, while Theorem 3.3 restricted to linear f(x); experiments use ReLU/softplus on varying-width networks, so theoretical guarantees don't apply

Marginal empirical improvements: CLAPP++ (80.51%) vs SCFF (80.60%) on CIFAR-10 within confidence intervals; STL-10 gap to BP-CLAPP++ remains 1.7%; improvements are modest given added complexity of spatial dependence

Biological plausibility claims overstated: Method still requires layer-wise loss functions and trained top-down feedback weights (B^l); credit assignment mechanism via neuromodulators remains speculative; advantages over BP for biological systems unclear

Limited practical scope: Only VGG architectures tested; scalability to modern ResNets and Vision Transformers unclear; only image classification evaluated; no actual runtime/memory quantification despite efficiency claims

Arbitrary algorithmic design choices: Spatial dependence structure (Table A2 patch sizes) appears ad-hoc; why 4×4 for CIFAR-10 vs 12×12 for STL-10 lacks principled justification; empirically motivated rather than theoretically grounded

Theory assumes unrealistic conditions: Separation of timescales (B^l instantaneously optimal) is strong; Definition 3.4 (optimal local-SSL) requires BP computation, defeating purpose for neuromorphic systems; L2 regularization required for convexity proof adds hyperparameter

Inconsistent comparisons: BP-InfoNCE baseline (80.69%) outperforms CLAPP++ (80.51%) on CIFAR-10, contradicting claims of matching BP-SSL; CLAPP++both uses combined loss reducing locality; limited analysis of why BP-approximation methods (DFA, PC) fail

strengths: Novel theoretical framework establishing exact equivalence between local-SSL and BP-SSL for deep linear networks with orthonormal weights (Theorem 3.1), along with unified formalism encompassing CLAPP, Forward-forward, PhyLL, and SCFF

Well-structured progression from theory to practice: linear networks → ReLU MLPs with direct feedback → convolutional networks with spatial dependence, effectively translating theoretical insights into practical algorithms
First demonstration that local-SSL can match global BP-SSL performance on standard benchmarks (CIFAR-10, STL-10, Tiny ImageNet)—a significant milestone for the local learning community

Rigorous numerical validation of theoretical predictions: Figure 2-4 show that removing conditions degrades alignment, and ablation studies (Table 2, Figure 5) clearly isolate contributions of algorithmic modifications
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, network architectures, training procedures in appendices; honest acknowledgment of limitations and fair comparisons with baselines
Thoughtful biological plausibility discussion connecting apical dendrites, neuromodulators, and structured connectivity to the learning rules in concrete, non-speculative ways
weaknesses: Theorem 3.1 applies only to unrealistic settings: requires orthonormal weight matrices (violated by standard initialization), equal layer widths, and linear networks—the main theoretical contribution has severely limited practical relevance

Substantial theory-practice gap: main theorem requires linear networks but practical improvements occur in non-linear networks; spatial dependence is introduced heuristically rather than rigorously derived from theory; Theorem 3.3 only applies when f is linear

Marginal empirical improvements within error bars: CIFAR-10 CLAPP++ (80.51±0.27) vs BP-CLAPP++ (80.49±0.20) statistically indistinguishable; STL-10 actually shows degradation (78.66 vs 80.36); claims of 'matching' performance overstate results

Missing computational efficiency analysis: no wall-clock time comparisons, FLOPs analysis, or hardware efficiency metrics despite efficiency being the primary motivation for local-SSL; claimed memory reduction for CLAPP++DFB is unquantified

Incomplete treatment of Forward-Forward algorithms: Theorem 3.1 does not extend to normalization-based algorithms despite FF variants being state-of-the-art; limited exploration of why theory breaks down

Spatial dependence implementation appears dataset-specific: Table A2 shows different patch sizes for different layers and datasets with limited justification; raises generalization concerns about the approach
Definition 3.4 (optimal local-SSL) requires computing BP gradients, defeating the purpose of a 'local' algorithm; undermines the theoretical motivation
Underexplored failure of BP-approximation methods: Appendix C shows Predictive Coding and DFA fail on SSL objectives, but limited analysis of why CLAPP succeeds where they fail

strengths: Strong theoretical contribution establishing that local-SSL can implement identical BP-SSL updates in deep linear networks with orthonormal weights, with systematic progression through related results (Theorem 3.1, Corollary 3.2, Theorem 3.3)
Algorithm design grounded in theory rather than ad-hoc; 2D spatial dependence improvements are theoretically justified (Proposition 3.5) and empirically validated
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets with proper baselines, ablation studies (Figure 5, Table 2), and statistical confidence intervals; state-of-the-art local-SSL results
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, architecture specifications, code availability, and systematic training procedures in appendix
Unified notation (Table 1) elegantly encompasses multiple local-SSL algorithms (CLAPP, Forward-Forward, PhyLL, SCFF), facilitating comparative analysis
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging gaps with mainstream SSL and architectural constraints, avoiding overclaiming impact
weaknesses: Large theory-practice gap: Theorem 3.1 requires orthonormal weights, linear networks, and equal layer widths, but all experiments use non-linear ReLU networks with random initialization. While Figure 2 shows graceful degradation, theoretical justification for why the algorithm works without these conditions is missing

Limited to VGG architectures; no ResNets or modern networks with residual connections and normalization layers. ImageNet gap (44.16% vs 48.52%) indicates method doesn't fully scale. Authors acknowledge residual connections are 'non-trivial challenge' but don't address this critical limitation

Marginal practical efficiency gains: VRAM reduction (38-60%) requires ideal algorithms not used in practice; actual Algorithm 3 uses stop-gradient. Wall-clock time (Table 3) shows minimal improvement (146ms vs 125ms for STL-10), undermining efficiency claims. Missing analysis of actual computational benefits

Theory-practice misalignment unresolved: Theorem 3.3 proves DFB helps with linear f but experiments use ReLU without theoretical justification. Proposition 3.5 requires patch size k₁=k₂=1 (prohibitive), but practical implementation uses k>1 without justified explanation

Non-standard evaluation procedure (multi-layer representation concatenation) makes direct comparison with other SSL methods difficult. BP baselines (BP-CLAPP++, BP-InfoNCE) not state-of-the-art; mainstream SSL uses ResNets with non-linear heads
Connection between gradient alignment and downstream performance assumed rather than justified. Why should approximate gradient matching to BP-SSL guarantee performance matching?
Biological plausibility claims remain speculative: requires trainable lateral matrices B^l, top-down signals from final layer, and precise learning rule coordination—less plausible than claimed

Missing critical analysis: Appendix D shows DFA and Predictive Coding fail on SSL objectives but doesn't explain why—this insight could strengthen core contribution. Limited ablation on batch size effects, hyperparameter sensitivity, or failure modes

strengths: Novel theoretical framework establishing exact equivalence between local-SSL and BP-SSL for linear networks (Theorem 3.1), with rigorous proofs and comprehensive numerical verification
Exemplary theory-to-practice pipeline: theoretical insights directly guide algorithmic improvements (spatial dependence, direct feedback) with consistent empirical validation at each step
Unified formalism (Table 1) encompassing CLAPP, Forward-forward, PhyLL, and SCFF—valuable contribution for organizing the local-SSL literature
Significant practical achievement: matching BP-SSL performance on CIFAR-10, STL-10, and TinyImageNet, addressing long-standing performance gaps in local learning
Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation with ablation studies, multiple datasets, comparison with state-of-the-art, numerical verification of theorems, and reproducible code
Thoughtful biological plausibility discussion connecting CLAPP++DFB to apical dendrite anatomy and 2D spatial structure to cortical connectivity patterns
Practical benefits including 40-60% VRAM reduction compared to BP-SSL, making local learning attractive for resource-constrained applications
Honest and nuanced limitations discussion, including empirical validation that spatial dependence helps local-SSL but not BP-SSL
weaknesses: Theoretical results severely limited to linear networks; extension to practical nonlinear networks is purely empirical, creating substantial gap between theory and practice
Theorem 3.1 requires orthonormal weight matrices, which is violated immediately after the first forward pass—practical relevance of this theoretical condition is unclear
Theorem 3.3 (direct feedback improvement) requires linear activation functions in proof, but empirically shows benefits with nonlinear activations; this theory-practice gap is inadequately explained
Theory does not extend to Forward-forward algorithms due to normalization requirements, significantly limiting scope given FF's prominence in local-SSL literature
Algorithm 3 (used in practice) differs substantially from ideal Algorithms 1-2: uses stop gradients to disable gradient flow, undermining 'local learning' claims and creating reproducibility concerns

Experimental scale modest by current standards: uses VGG rather than ResNet, and ImageNet results remain substantially weaker (44.16% vs 48.52% for BP—4.36% gap), suggesting potential fundamental limitations at scale
Requires dataset-specific hyperparameter tuning for spatial dependence patch sizes (Table A2), with no principled method for setting these for new domains—undermines biological plausibility claims
Forward-forward performance gains over prior SOTA (SCFF) are modest (78.66% vs 77.14% on STL-10, only 1.52% improvement), limiting practical impact claims
Spatial dependence intuition underdeveloped: why it specifically helps local-SSL relative to BP-SSL remains largely unexplained beyond technical analysis

Biological plausibility claims weakened by several factors: discrete neuromodulator values (γ ∈ {−1, 0, 1}), unconstrained B^l search space, and lack of clear principled way to select spatial patch sizes
